themes.consensus_view: Most desks read the Fed's quarter-point September hike and its own rate projections as the start of more increases, while Rabobank argues this was a one-off, so the open question is how much more tightening actually lands.

facts_agreed.claim: The September FOMC came out more hawkish than expected and the banks expect at least one more hike.
evidence_quotes: This hike helps the Fed rebuild credibility as an inflation fighter.
Today’s meeting is consistent with our outlook for another hike in December
The SEP shifted in a notably hawkish direction reflecting a stronger growth and labor market outlook
We now expect the FOMC to deliver a second 25bp hike in October

facts_agreed.claim: Policy is only now approaching the rate the banks consider neutral, so conditions are not yet tight.
evidence_quotes: rate expectations are knocking on the door of the neutral rate.

facts_agreed.claim: Desks that publish a rate path put themselves at or above the Fed's own median projection.
evidence_quotes: PNC’s fed funds rate forecast is consistent with the median dot through the end of 2026
Today’s meeting is consistent with our outlook for another hike in December

facts_contested.claim: how many more hikes this cycle delivers
facts_contested.for_evidence: markets have a tendency to underestimate the scale of Fed hiking cycles at the start.
facts_contested.against_evidence: we still think it is more likely that this turns out to be a “one and done” hike

themes.consensus_view: Every desk covering this theme says spending on AI computing and data centers is still accelerating, with the debate no longer about whether demand holds up but about how the build-out gets paid for and whether the returns show up before companies cut back.

facts_agreed.claim: AI infrastructure demand is still strong and spending shows no sign of slowing.
evidence_quotes: Investment in artificial intelligence (AI) infrastructure shows no sign of slowing.
continued pushback against concerns slower pace of AI model development will meaningfully impact demand
AI demand remains robust, as evidenced by continued earnings revisions across the sector
demand trends are still strong. During the recent earnings season, we saw signs

facts_agreed.claim: Data center growth is pulling spending toward electricity supply, which has replaced chips as the binding constraint.
evidence_quotes: We expect significant growth in AI data centers to drive a strong increase
The company sees the AI datacenter bottleneck shifting from compute to power delivery

facts_agreed.claim: The largest cloud companies are now spending more than their own cash generation supports and are funding the gap in the bond and equity markets.
evidence_quotes: The surge in capex spending among the hyperscalers has increasingly eaten through their free cash flow

facts_agreed.claim: Investors are paying up for the profitable hardware and data center side of AI while stepping back from the speculative end.
evidence_quotes: a clear split between profitable/duration AI and the speculative cohort.
the market favoured profitable infrastructure exposure, including data centres and AI semis

themes.consensus_view: Six desks treat new Fed Chair Warsh's Jackson Hole remarks and his public communication as a live policy question after the September rate hike, but none of them stakes out a directional call on what he will say or do.

facts_agreed.claim: Six banks reference Warsh's Jackson Hole speech and his Fed communication as an upcoming policy event to watch in this window.
evidence_quotes: Fed Chair Warsh Jackson Hole speech

facts_agreed.claim: Several desks frame the new Fed chair's credibility and the resulting uncertainty about the policy path as the reason the speech matters.

themes.consensus_view: Five desks flag the US-Iran conflict and the threat to oil shipments through the Strait of Hormuz as a live driver of crude prices, but none has committed to a direction for oil.

facts_agreed.claim: Five banks treat the Middle East conflict as an active risk to oil and commodity prices without staking a directional call.
evidence_quotes: Middle East conflict oil price impact
Strait of Hormuz energy flow disruptions

facts_agreed.claim: UBS repeatedly links the US-Iran conflict to the path of Fed interest rate policy, not just to energy supply.
evidence_quotes: US-Iran war impact on policy rates
US-Iran war escalation impact on Fed policy

themes.consensus_view: Four desks flag the US midterm elections as a live backdrop for fiscal policy and seasonal stock patterns, but none has taken a side on what the vote means for markets.

facts_agreed.claim: Four banks reference the US midterm elections as an upcoming policy and seasonal backdrop without arguing a market direction.
evidence_quotes: US fiscal position and midterm elections

themes.consensus_view: Most of the desks expect stocks to keep grinding higher on strong company profits even as the Fed raises rates, while Goldman Sachs sits on the sidelines for the next three months because of risk in the bond market.

facts_agreed.claim: The equity rally has room to run over the next six to twelve months because stocks have already taken the recent bad news.
evidence_quotes: we believe the equity rally will continue over the next six to 12 months.
Equities have already absorbed a slew of negative catalysts over the last few weeks

facts_agreed.claim: Company profits, not cheaper money, are the engine behind the move in global stocks.
evidence_quotes: Earnings, supported by structural and cyclical trends, should drive global equities higher
Asian equities remain attractive, supported by solid earnings, reasonable valuations and durable AI-related demand.

facts_agreed.claim: A gradual Fed rate-hiking cycle is not treated as enough on its own to end the rally.
evidence_quotes: we do not expect a measured Fed tightening cycle to derail the equity rally.

facts_contested.claim: whether to add equity risk now or wait out the next three months
facts_contested.for_evidence: we believe the equity rally will continue over the next six to 12 months.
facts_contested.against_evidence: we remain neutral on equities, alongside other asset classes on a 3-month horizon

facts_contested.claim: whether Fed tightening is a threat to the equity rally
facts_contested.for_evidence: we do not expect a measured Fed tightening cycle to derail the equity rally.
facts_contested.against_evidence: we remain neutral on equities, alongside other asset classes on a 3-month horizon

themes.consensus_view: Three desks are tracking how fast the big cloud companies keep raising their spending on AI data centers, and how they pay for it, but none of them has staked out a bullish or bearish call on the spending itself.

facts_agreed.claim: Three desks treat the pace of hyperscaler capital spending as a live subject this window without taking a directional view on it.
The Market Ear frames the subject specifically as a slowdown in the rate of spending growth rather than an outright drop in spending.
UBS and Goldman Sachs both raise how the spending is funded, pointing at bond sales and at the cash left over after the spending.

themes.consensus_view: Three desks flag the Saudi East-West pipeline as a live oil supply story this week, with Goldman describing it as an outage and a disruption, but none of them has committed to a direction for oil prices off it.

facts_agreed.claim: Three banks reference the Saudi East-West pipeline as a current oil supply headline without taking a directional view on it.
Goldman Sachs frames the pipeline as a supply disruption and an outage rather than a capacity question.
